AC "refuses in CI" is unimplemented: `gate_decide.py`/`gate_decisions.py` have no CI environment detection; any CI job can pass `--hil-confirmed`.

AC "approval treats SCOPE findings as resolved only with a follow-up item" / "SCOPE findings are non-blocking and must reference a follow-up item": only `DISPOSITION_STATUSES` gained "SCOPE"; `gate2_status()` and approval logic are untouched, so SCOPE has no semantics, no follow-up linkage, and no non-blocking behaviour.
Required tests are missing: no gate0 positive/negative test, no SCOPE-resolution test, no accepted-risk validation test, no duplicate-review-refusal test (`architect_review.py` change is untested).

Traceability/integrity: the diff for BI-PF-1471 delivers a large, unrelated BI-PF-1308 object-lifecycle/signed-URL change (Go packages, ADR EDP-16) with no corresponding AC; two work items are conflated in one change.
MAJOR: `gate0_check.py` fails open: if `git merge-base develop HEAD` or `origin/develop` is unavailable (shallow CI clone), `_git` returns "", diff yields zero transitions, and the blocking gate prints `gate0: OK` — a vacuous pass for a blocking gate.

`go_modules_check.py::_git_changed` swallows all exceptions and returns `[]`, so a git failure makes `_changed_modules` empty and the gate reports "no Go changes", skipping formatting/vet/tests for all modules (fail-open).
AC "gate-brief renders the same for HIL" is not implemented: `gate0_check.render()` is only used by the precheck path; no gate-brief integration exists.

Precheck test-selection regression: `_steps` now runs no Python tests at all when `_python_impact` is false and removes the previous "no scope match → full suite" fallback, reducing coverage for transitive breakage.

Parallelising gates (`ThreadPoolExecutor`, `parallel_safe`) is risky: the set includes gates (e.g. `docs-fresh`, `wired-audit`) that may emit/write derived artifacts; concurrent writers and interleaved output undermine the "read-only" claim and observability.
`LocalStore.keyLocks` grows unboundedly per key for the process lifetime (no eviction), a slow memory leak in a long-lived service.

Duplicate-review guard in `architect_review.py` checks existence of `EVID/{item}-{sha}.json` before writing; correctness depends on the (unshown) writer using the identical naming and on `design_sha`/`diff_sha` being the same immutable inputs — no test guards the invariant.

`--hil-confirmed` as a `required=True` store_true is trivially satisfiable by any automation; the actor binding (`--by hil:<actor>`) is self-asserted, so human-only intent is convention, not control.
Gate0 transition detection treats any prior-status≠in_progress as a transition (e.g. blocked→in_progress), broader than the AC's new→in_progress; document or narrow.
`S3Store.Capabilities()` acquires the mutex twice, yielding a non-atomic snapshot of `objectLock`/`versioned`; fold into one critical section.
New `errors.Is` usage in `objstore.go` — the import line is not shown in the diff; confirm compilation (no `errors` import added).

`deny()`'s overflow bucket overwrites an existing `_overflow|reason` key semantics; counters are process-local only — no metrics export, so "denials counted per tenant+reason" is not operationally observable.
`TestScanAbortsOnTransientHeadError` contains dead setup (`st` assigned then discarded), hurting test readability/maintenance.
NIT: `log.Printf` inside library packages (`objpolicy`, `objreconcile`, `s3store`) bypasses structured logging conventions; consider an injected logger.
Trailing blank line added at EOF of `go_modules_check.py`.
`gate_decisions.record_gate_decision` hard-codes `"hil_confirmed": True` in the record rather than recording who/what confirmed, reducing audit fidelity.
objreconcile `Entry.Checksum` empty means "size-only"; a manifest typo silently downgrades verification — consider flagging it instead of accepting.
SUMMARY: The delivered diff does not satisfy BI-PF-1471: accepted-risk validation, CI refusal, and the SCOPE scope-guard semantics are missing, and all AC-required tests are absent; the substantial Go object-lifecycle work (BI-PF-1308) is unrelated scope bundled into this item.
The pieces that exist (gate0 check + precheck wiring, duplicate-review refusal, `--hil-confirmed`) are sound in shape but fail open under git/CI conditions and lack tests.

Top risks: blocking gates that pass vacuously, reduced precheck test coverage plus concurrent gate execution, and an unenforced SCOPE disposition that could silently let unaddressed findings through Gate 2.
